```sql

```sql
SELECT
  carrier,
  CAST(on_time / flown AS REAL) * 100 AS share_on_time
FROM
  turnaround.mart_carrier_month
WHERE
  year = 2016
ORDER BY
  share_on_time DESC
LIMIT 1;

```sql
SELECT carrier, on_time / SUM(on_time) * 100 AS on_time_share
FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month
WHERE year = 2016
WHERE carrier = 'B6' OR carrier = 'UA'
GROUP BY carrier
ORDER BY on_time_share DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN T2.on_time > T1.on_time THEN 'United'
        WHEN T1.on_time > T2.on_time THEN 'JetBlue'
        ELSE 'Equal'
    END AS has更高的 share of flights on time in 2016, United OR JetBlue
FROM 
    turnaround.export_ch3_by_carrier AS T1
JOIN 
    turnaround.export_ch1_by_year AS T2 ON T2.carrier = T1.carrier AND T2.year = 2016
WHERE 
    T1.carrier = 'B6' OR T1.carrier = 'UA'
ORDER BY 
    has更高的 share of flights on time in 2016, United OR JetBlue DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    "carrier" AS label,
    (ON_time / Flights) * 100 AS value
FROM 
    turnaround.export_ch5_ranking
WHERE 
    year = 2016
ORDER BY 
    value DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN T1.on_time / (T1.scheduled - T1.cancelled) > T2.on_time / (T2.scheduled - T2.cancelled) THEN 'United' ELSE 'JetBlue' END AS WhoHadHigherShare
FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T1
JOIN turnaround.export_ch1_by_year AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year
WHERE T1.year = 2016

```sql
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN (SELECT CAST(flights AS REAL) * 100 / total_flights FROM turnaround.export_ch1_by_year WHERE year = 2016 AND carrier = 'B6') > (SELECT CAST(flights AS REAL) * 100 / total_flights FROM turnaround.export_ch1_by_year WHERE year = 2016 AND carrier = 'UA') THEN 'United'
        ELSE 'JetBlue'
    END AS result
FROM
    turnaround.export_ch1_by_year

    (SELECT SUM(flights) AS total_flights FROM turnaround.export_ch1_by_year WHERE year = 2016) AS total
ON
    1 = 1

```sql
SELECT 
    IF(DL_airport_avg > OO_airport_avg, 'Delta Air Lines', 'OO') AS higher_average_airport,
    IF(DL_airport_avg > OO_airport_avg, DL_airport_avg, OO_airport_avg) AS average_airport_delay
FROM (
    SELECT 
        airport, 
        SUM(arr_delay_sum) / COUNT(*) AS airport_avg

        turnaround.mart_airport_day
    WHERE 
        year = 2017

        carrier IN ('DL', 'OO')

```sql
SELECT 
    T2.carrier,
    AVG(T1.arr_delay_sum) AS average_arrival_delay
FROM 
    turnaround.mart_airport_day AS T1
LEFT JOIN 
    turnaround.export_ch6_nas_by_airport AS T2
ON 
    T1.airport = T2.Airport AND T1.year = T2.Year
WHERE 
    T1.year = 2017
    AND T2.carrier IN ('DL', 'OO')
GROUP BY 
    T2.carrier
ORDER BY 
    average_arrival_delay DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH flight_delays AS (
    SELECT
        YEAR(flight_date) AS year,
        carrier,
        SUM(arr_delay_sum) / COUNT(*) AS avg_arr_delay
    FROM
        turnaround.export_ch6_reported_by_year
    WHERE
        year = 2017
    GROUP BY
        YEAR(flight_date),
        carrier
),
delta_air_lines AS (
    SELECT
        'DL' AS carrier,
        avg_arr_delay
    FROM
        flight_delays
    WHERE
        carrier = 'DL'
),
oo_airlines AS (
    SELECT
        'OO' AS carrier,
        avg_arr_delay
    FROM
        flight_delays
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN delta_air_lines.avg_arr_delay > oo_airlines.avg_arr_delay THEN 'Delta Air Lines'
        WHEN delta_air_lines.avg_arr_delay < oo_airlines.avg_arr_delay THEN 'OO'
        ELSE 'REFUSE'
        AND 'NO_SUCH_MEASURE'
    END AS result
FROM
    delta_air_lines
JOIN
    oo_airlines
ON
    1 = 1;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE WHEN T1.avg_arr_delay > T2.avg_arr_delay THEN 'Delta Air Lines' ELSE 'OO' END AS Warehouse,
    T2.avg_arr_delay AS Average_Arr_Delay
FROM 
    (SELECT 
         COUNT(carrier) AS flights_count,
         AVG(arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arr_delay
     FROM 
         turnaround.mart_carrier_month
     WHERE 
         year = 2017 AND carrier = 'DL'
     GROUP BY 
         year) T1
JOIN 
    (SELECT 
         COUNT(carrier) AS flights_count,
         AVG(arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arr_delay
     FROM 
         turnaround.mart_carrier_month
     WHERE 
         year = 2017 AND carrier = 'OO'
     GROUP BY 
         year) T2;
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN doorstep.mart_metro_year.cbsa_title = 'Lafayette, LA' THEN CASE WHEN doorstep.mart_metro_year.permits > doorstep.fct_metro_year.permits THEN 'Higher' ELSE 'Lower' END
    WHEN doorstep.mart_metro_year.cbsa_title = 'Omaha, NE-IA' THEN CASE WHEN doorstep.mart_metro_year.permits > doorstep.fct_metro_year.permits THEN 'Higher' ELSE 'Lower' END
    ELSE 'REFUSE, PERSON'
  END AS result
FROM 
  doorstep.mart_metro_year
JOIN 
  doorstep.fct_metro_year
ON 
  doorstep.mart_metro_year.cbsa_code = doorstep.fct_metro_year.cbsa_code AND doorstep.mart_metro_year.year = doorstep.fct_metro_year.year
WHERE 
  doorstep.mart_metro_year.year = 2014;
```

```sql

    CASE
        WHEN T1.housing_units > T2.housing_units THEN 'Lafayette, LA'
        WHEN T1.housing_units < T2.housing_units THEN 'Omaha, NE-IA'
        ELSE 'No difference in permitted housing units'
    END AS result,
    T1.housing_units AS Lafayette_housing_units,
    T2.housing_units AS Omaha_housing_units
FROM
    doorstep.fct_metro_year AS T1
LEFT JOIN
    doorstep.fct_metro_year AS T2
ON
    T1.cbsa_code = T2.cbsa_code AND T1.year = 2014 AND T2.year = 2014 AND T2.cbsa_title = 'Lafayette, LA';
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN sum(case when group = 'Hispanic or Latino' then rate end) > 
         sum(case when group = 'Other or joint' then rate end) AND
         sum(case when group = 'Hispanic or Latino' then rate end) > 
         sum(case when group = 'Other or joint' then rate end) THEN 'Hispanic or Latino'
    WHEN sum(case when group = 'Other or joint' then rate end) > 
         sum(case when group = 'Other or joint' then rate end) AND
         sum(case when group = 'Hispanic or Latino' then rate end) < 
         sum(case when group = 'Other or joint' then rate end) THEN 'Other or joint'
    ELSE 'Hispanic or Latino' 
  END AS group, 
  sum(case when group = 'Hispanic or Latino' then rate end) AS rate
FROM 
  ledger.f03_denial_reasons
GROUP BY 
  group
ORDER BY 
  rate DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH avg_arrival_delays AS (
  SELECT 
    carrier AS label,
    AVG(arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arrival_delay
  FROM 
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
  WHERE 
    year = 2018
    AND carrier IN ('YX', 'WN')
  GROUP BY 
    carrier

  CASE 
    WHEN avg_arrival_delay_1 > avg_arrival_delay_2 THEN 'YX'
    ELSE 'WN'
  END AS label,

  avg_arrival_delays AS avg_arrival_delays_1

  avg_arrival_delays AS avg_arrival_delays_2

  avg_arrival_delays_1.label = avg_arrival_delays_2.label

  avg_arrival_delays_1.year = 2018
  AND avg_arrival_delays_2.year = 2018;

JOIN turnaround.mart_carrier_flight_sum AS T3 ON T1.carrier = T3.carrier AND T1.year = T3.year
WHERE T1.year = 2018

HAVING AVG(T3.arr_delay_sum) / 60 > (SELECT AVG(arr_delay_sum) / 60 FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month WHERE year = 2018 AND carrier = 'YX')

        WHEN T1.year = 2018 AND T2.year = 2018 AND T1.on_time < T2.on_time THEN 'Southwest'
        ELSE 'REFUSE: NO_DATA'

    turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T1

```sql
SELECT CASE
    WHEN t1.alerts > t2.alerts THEN 1
    WHEN t1.alerts < t2.alerts THEN -1
    ELSE 0 END AS precision_diff_percentage
FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN ledger.f05_rule_scorecard t2 ON t1.rule = 'rapid_movement' AND t2.rule = 'structuring'
WHERE t1.alerts IS NOT NULL AND t2.alerts IS NOT NULL;
```

```sql
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN t2.precision > t1.precision THEN 'rapid_movement'
    ELSE 'structuring'
  END AS rule_with_larger_precision,
  (t2.precision - t1.precision) * 100 / t1.precision AS precision_difference_percent
FROM
  ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN
  ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard t2 ON t1.rule = t2.rule
WHERE
  t1.rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring') AND t2.rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring')
ORDER BY
  precision_difference_percent DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN t2.precision * 100 > t1.precision * 100 THEN 'rapid_movement'
        ELSE 'structuring'
    END AS rule,
    (t2.precision * 100) AS precision
FROM 
    ledger.f04_label_lag t1
JOIN 
    ledger.f04_pr_curve t2 ON t1.day = t2.threshold
WHERE 
    t1.rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring')
ORDER BY 
    precision DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN T3.precision > T4.precision THEN 'rapid_movement'
        ELSE 'structuring'
    END AS rule,
    T3.precision * 100 AS precision_percentage
FROM 
    ledger.f05_rule_scorecard AS T1
JOIN 
    ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard AS T2
ON 
    T1.rule = T2.rule
JOIN 
    ledger.f04_label_lag AS T3
ON 
    T1.rule = T3.rule
JOIN 
    ledger.f04_pr_curve AS T4
ON 
    T1.rule = T4.rule AND T1.alerts = T4.threshold
WHERE 
    T1.rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring');
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN rule = 'rapid_movement' THEN round(100 * precision, 2)
    ELSE round(100 * (1 - precision), 2)
  END AS alert_precision_percent
FROM 
  ledger.f05_rule_scorecard
WHERE 
  rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring')
ORDER BY 
  alert_precision_percent DESC
LIMIT 1
```

```sql
SELECT CASE 
        WHEN t1.true_positives / t1.alerts * 100 > t2.true_positives / t2.alerts THEN 'rapid movement'
        ELSE 'structuring'
    END AS alert_precision_percent
FROM ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t2 ON t1.rule = 'rapid_movement' AND t2.rule = 'structuring'
ORDER BY alert_precision_percent DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN (SELECT precision FROM ledger.f04_label_lag WHERE threshold = rapid_movement) > (SELECT precision FROM ledger.f04_label_lag WHERE threshold = structuring) THEN rapid_movement
        ELSE structuring
    END AS rule_with_larger_precision
FROM ledger.f04_label_lag
WHERE precision >= 0.5;
```

```sql

       CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN rule = 'structuring' THEN true_positives ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) * 100 / SUM(true_positives) AS structuring_percentage

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN AS_cancelled_rate > NK_cancelled_rate THEN 'AS'
    WHEN NK_cancelled_rate > AS_cancelled_rate THEN 'NK'
    ELSE 'NO SUCH MEASURE'
  END AS entity_or_period,
  AS_cancelled_rate - NK_cancelled_rate AS difference
FROM (
  SELECT 
    YEAR AS year,
    CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN STATUS = 'C' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100 AS AS_cancelled_rate
  FROM 
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
  WHERE 
    Carrier = 'AS'
    AND YEAR = 2018
  GROUP BY 
    YEAR
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    YEAR AS year,
    CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN STATUS = 'C' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100 AS NK_cancelled_rate
  FROM 
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
  WHERE 
    Carrier = 'NK'
    AND YEAR = 2018
  GROUP BY 
    YEAR
) AS subquery
WHERE 
  difference > 0;
```

Let's write the SQL query to find the larger mean arrival delay between Alaska Airlines and American in 2017:

```sql
WITH filtered_tables AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN carrier = 'AS' THEN 'Alaska Airlines' ELSE 'American' END as entity,
        year,
        month,
        on_time,
        mean_arr_delay
    FROM
        turnaround.mart_carrier_month
    WHERE
        year = 2017
),
average_delays AS (
    SELECT
        entity,
        month,
        AVG(mean_arr_delay) as average_mean_arr_delay
    FROM
        filtered_tables
    GROUP BY
        entity,
        month
)
SELECT
    entity,
    month,
    CASE
        WHEN average_mean_arr_delay_1 > average_mean_arr_delay_2 THEN 'Alaska Airlines'
        ELSE 'American'
    END as larger_mean_arr_delay
FROM
    average_delays
ORDER BY
    average_mean_arr_delay_1 DESC, average_mean_arr_delay_2 DESC;
```

        year,
        quarter,
        rate AS black_rate
    FROM 
        ledger.f03_denial_reasons
    WHERE 
        group = 'Black'
),
hispanic_or_latino_application_rate AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        quarter,
        rate AS hispanic_or_latino_rate
    FROM 
        ledger.f03_denial_reasons
    WHERE 
        group = 'Hispanic or Latino'
)
SELECT 
    MAX(black_rate) AS max_black_rate,
    MAX(hispanic_or_latino_rate) AS max_hispanic_or_latino_rate
FROM 
    black_application_rate
JOIN 
    hispanic_or_latino_application_rate ON black_application_rate.year = hispanic_or_latino_application_rate.year AND black_application_rate.quarter = hispanic_or_latino_application_rate.quarter;
```

```sql

    CASE 
        WHEN cancelled_envoy / (cancelled_envoy + flown_envoy) > cancelled_alaska / (cancelled_alaska + flown_alaska) THEN 'Envoy'
        ELSE 'Alaska Airlines'
    END AS cancellation_rate_larger,
    CASE 
        WHEN cancelled_envoy / (cancelled_envoy + flown_envoy) > cancelled_alaska / (cancelled_alaska + flown_alaska) THEN 'Envoy'
        ELSE 'Alaska Airlines'

    cancelled_envoy AS cancelled_envoy,

WHERE
    mcm_envoy.year = 2023 AND mcm_alaska.year = 2023

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN T1.avg_arr_delay > T2.avg_arr_delay THEN 'Mesa'
    WHEN T1.avg_arr_delay < T2.avg_arr_delay THEN 'JetBlue'
    ELSE 'EQUALS'
  END AS result
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('year', T1.flight_date) AS year,
    AVG(T1.arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arr_delay
  FROM
    turnaround.mart_airport_day AS T1
  WHERE
    T1.carrier = 'YV'
    AND DATE_TRUNC('year', T1.flight_date) = 2020
  GROUP BY
    year
) AS T1
JOIN (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('year', T2.flight_date) AS year,
    AVG(T2.arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arr_delay
  FROM
    turnaround.mart_airport_day AS T2
  WHERE
    T2.carrier = 'B6'
    AND DATE_TRUNC('year', T2.flight_date) = 2020
  GROUP BY
    year
) AS T2
ON T1.year = T2.year;

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN t2.precision > t3.precision THEN 'mule'
        ELSE 'structuring'
    END AS alert_precision
FROM 
    ledger.models_aml_triage_scored AS t1
JOIN 
    ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard AS t2 ON t1.rule = t2.rule
JOIN 
    ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard AS t3 ON t1.rule = t3.rule
WHERE 
    t1.rule IN ('mule', 'structuring')
ORDER BY 
    alert_precision DESC;
```

This query joins the three relevant tables to compare the alert precision of 'money mule' and 'structuring' rules. It uses a CASE statement to determine which alert precision is larger and returns it as the result.

```sql
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN 'money mule'
    ELSE 'structuring'
  END AS rule,
  MAX(t1.precision) AS alert_precision
FROM
  ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN
  ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard t2
ON
  t1.rule = 'mule' AND t2.rule = 'structuring'
```

```sql
SELECT CASE 
       WHEN lms.precision > smms.precision THEN 'money mule'
       WHEN lms.precision < smms.precision THEN 'structuring'
       ELSE 'refuse out_of_scope' END AS entity_or_period,
       lms.precision AS alert_precision
FROM ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard lms JOIN ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard smms ON lms.rule = smms.rule
WHERE lms.rule IN ('mule', 'structuring');
```

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN 'mule' ELSE 'structuring' END AS rule, 
       SUM(CASE WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN t1.alerts ELSE t2.alerts END) AS more_alerts,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN t2.alerts ELSE t1.alerts END) AS fewer_alerts
FROM ledger.models_aml_triage_alerts_scored AS t1
JOIN ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard AS t2 ON t1.rule = t2.rule
WHERE t1.rule = 'mule' OR t1.rule = 'structuring'
GROUP BY t1.rule
ORDER BY more_alerts DESC;
```

```sql
WITH alert_precision AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN rule = 'mule' THEN precision
            ELSE precision
        END AS precision
    FROM
        ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard
),
merged_alerts AS (
    SELECT
        day,
        CASE
            WHEN rule = 'mule' THEN alerts
            ELSE SUM(alerts) OVER (PARTITION BY day)
        END AS total_alerts,
        CASE
            WHEN rule = 'mule' THEN true_positives
            ELSE SUM(true_positives) OVER (PARTITION BY day)
        END AS total_true_positives
    FROM
        ledger.models_aml_triage_alerts_scored
)
SELECT
    day,
    CASE
        WHEN total_alerts > total_true_positives THEN 'money mule'
        ELSE 'structuring'
    END AS alert_precision
FROM
    merged_alerts
ORDER BY
    day DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN 'money mule' ELSE 'structuring' END AS which_has_larger_alert_precision
FROM 
  ledger.f05_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN 
  ledger.f05_rule_scorecard t2
ON 
  t1.rule = 'mule' AND t2.rule = 'structuring'
```

```sql
SELECT CASE 
           WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN 'mule'
           WHEN t1.precision < t2.precision THEN 'structuring'
           ELSE 'equal'
       END AS alert_precision
FROM ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard t2
ON t1.rule = 'mule' AND t2.rule = 'structuring'
ORDER BY alert_precision DESC
```

```sql
WITH_json AS (
  SELECT
    cbsa_title AS city,
    CAST(
      CAST(ch3_burden_by_income[0].renters_with_share[0] AS DOUBLE) * 100 AS REAL
    ) AS share
  FROM
    doorstep.ch3_burden_by_income
  WHERE
    year = 2011
  AND
    city IN ('Jackson, MS', 'Killeen-Temple, TX')
),
city_vs_city AS (
  SELECT
    city,
    COALESCE(json[0].share, 0) AS city_share,
    COALESCE(json[1].share, 0) AS neighbor_share,
    city_share - neighbor_share AS share_diff
  FROM
    with_json
)
SELECT
  city,
  share_diff,
  CASE
    WHEN share_diff > 0 THEN 'Higher'
    ELSE 'Lower'
  END AS greater_than,
  CASE
    WHEN city_share > neighbor_share THEN 1
    ELSE -1
  END AS city_value,
  CASE
    WHEN neighbor_share > city_share THEN 1
    ELSE -1
  END AS neighbor_value
FROM
  city_vs_city;

    WHERE

        AND j.cbsa_title = 'Jackson, MS'

    SELECT

        j.mr AS j_mr,
        k.mr AS k_mr

-- Step 1: Join the turnaround table with the export_ch3_by_carrier table on the carrier column

```sql
WITH BlackOtherOrJoint AS (
    SELECT 
        CASE WHEN group = 'Black' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_black,
        CASE WHEN group = 'Other or joint' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_other_or_joint,
        ledger.rate
    FROM 
        ledger.f03_denial_reasons
    WHERE 
        race_ethnicity_group IN ('Black', 'Other or joint')
),
TotalBlackOtherOrJoint AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(is_black) AS black_count,
        SUM(is_other_or_joint) AS other_or_joint_count,
        SUM(rate) AS total_rate
    FROM 
        BlackOtherOrJoint
)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN total_black_other_or_joint.black_count > total_black_other_or_joint.other_or_joint_count THEN 'Black'
        ELSE 'Other or joint'
    END AS group_name,
    total_black_other_or_joint.total_rate AS denial_rate
FROM 
    TotalBlackOtherOrJoint
ORDER BY 
    denial_rate DESC;

        group,
        SUM(rate) AS total_rate

    GROUP BY

),
combined AS (

            WHEN black_other_or_joint.total_rate > other_or_joint.total_rate THEN 'Black'
            ELSE 'Other or joint'
        END AS result,
        black_other_or_joint.total_rate AS rate
    FROM

)

    WHERE carrier = 'YX'

)

         FROM Allegiant_flights)

         FROM YX_flights)
END AS percentage
FROM Allegiant_flights
JOIN YX_flights ON TRUE

```sql
SELECT

        WHEN `on_time`_HIGH < `on_time`_LOW THEN 'L'
        ELSE 'E'
    END AS result,
    `on_time`_HIGH / `on_time`_LOW AS ratio
FROM 
    (SELECT 
         carrier,
         SUM(CASE WHEN on_time = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `on_time`_HIGH,
         SUM(CASE WHEN on_time = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `on_time`_LOW
      FROM 
         turnover.mart_carrier_month

    needed AS on_time_rate_1,
    expected AS on_time_rate_2
FROM (

        SUM((flown - diverted) / on_time) AS needed,
        SUM(1 - (cancelled / on_time)) AS expected

    WHERE 
        carrier IN ('AS', 'UA') AND year = 2025
) t
ORDER BY 
    difference DESC

    ELSE `cancelled`
  END AS `value`

        WHEN on_time_rate_ha < on_time_rate_yx THEN on_time_rate_yx - on_time_rate_ha

```sql

Let's walk through the question and the available data.

To answer this question, we need to calculate the average arrival delay for both American Airlines (AA) and Mesa Airlines (YV) in 2018. Since the question asks for the average, we need to sum the arrival delays for each airline and then divide by the number of flights. The `arr_delay_sum` column in the `turnaround.mart_carrier_month` table contains the arrival delay for each flight.

Here's the SQL query to calculate the average arrival delay for both airlines:

```sql
SELECT 
    SUM(CASE WHEN carrier = 'AA' THEN arr_delay_sum ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN carrier = 'AA' THEN arr_delay_sum ELSE NULL END) AS avg_arr_delay_aa,
    SUM(CASE WHEN carrier = 'YV' THEN arr_delay_sum ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN carrier = 'YV' THEN arr_delay_sum ELSE NULL END) AS avg_arr_delay_yv
FROM 
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
WHERE 
    year = 2018;
```

```sql
WITH 
  structuring_precision AS (
    SELECT 
      rule, 
      SUM(true_positives) AS true_positive_sum,
      SUM(alerts) AS alerts_sum,
      SUM(true_positive_sum) / SUM(alerts_sum) AS precision
    FROM 
      ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard
    WHERE 
      rule = 'structuring'
    GROUP BY 
      rule
  ),
  rapid_movement_precision AS (
    SELECT 
      rule, 
      SUM(true_positives) AS true_positive_sum,
      SUM(alerts) AS alerts_sum,
      SUM(true_positive_sum) / SUM(alerts_sum) AS precision
    FROM 
      ledger.models_aml_triage_rule_scorecard
    WHERE 
      rule = 'rapid_movement'
    GROUP BY 
      rule
  )
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN structuring_precision.precision > rapid_movement_precision.precision THEN structuring_precision.rule
    ELSE rapid_movement_precision.rule
  END AS rule
FROM 
  structuring_precision
JOIN 
  rapid_movement_precision ON structuring_precision.rule = rapid_movement_precision.rule;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN sum(true_positives) / sum(episodes) > sum(true_positives) / sum(episodes_found) THEN 'structuring'
        ELSE 'rapid_movement'
    END AS rule, 
    sum(true_positives) / sum(episodes) AS precision
FROM 
    ledger.f04_label_lag
```

```sql

JOIN ledger.f04_label_lag AS T2 ON T1.threshold = T2.threshold
JOIN ledger.f05_rule_scorecard AS T3 ON T3.rule = 'rapid_movement' OR T3.rule = 'structuring'
WHERE T3.alerts > 0
ORDER BY precision DESC

```sql
SELECT
    CASE WHEN t1.precision >= t2.precision THEN 'STRUCTURING' ELSE 'RAPID_MOVEMENT' END AS rule,
    t1.precision AS precision
FROM
    ledger.f04_label_lag t1
LEFT JOIN
    ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t2
ON
    t1.day = t2.day AND t2.rule = 'STRICT_STRUCTURING';

```sql

        WHEN t1.precision >= t2.precision THEN 'rule_structuring'
        ELSE 'rule_rapid_movement'
    END AS rule, 
    t2.precision AS precision
FROM 
    ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t1
JOIN 
    ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t2 ON t1.rule = t2.rule
WHERE 
    t2.rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'structuring');
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN t1.precision < t2.precision THEN 'rapid_movement'
        WHEN t1.precision > t2.precision THEN 'structuring'
        ELSE 'equal'
    END AS rule_with_higher_precision,
    t1.precision AS rapid_movement_precision,
    t2.precision AS structuring_precision
FROM 
    ledger.f04_label_lag t1
JOIN 
    ledger.f04_rule_scorecard t2 ON t1.decisions = t2.alerts
WHERE 
    t1.decisions > 0;
```

  period,
  CASE WHEN Asian.application_rate > Other_or_joint.application_rate THEN Asian GROUP ELSE Other_or_joint GROUP END AS outcome

  (SELECT percentile_cont(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY applications) OVER (PARTITION BY group) AS application_rate FROM ledger.f03_denial_reasons WHERE race_ethnicity_group = 'Asian') AS Asian

WHERE
  outcome = 'Asian';

SELECT

    WHEN ledger.f03_denial_reasons.group = 'Not provided' THEN ledger.f03_denial_reasons.reason
    ELSE 'REFUSE'

    WHEN ledger.f03_denial_reasons.group = 'Not provided' THEN ledger.f03_denial_reasons.share * 100
    ELSE 'REFUSE'
  END AS denial_rate_percent

    CASE

Let's answer this question by combining data from multiple warehouses to get the median home price for both cities in 2023 in thousands of dollars. We'll use the `doorstep.ch8_metros` and `doorstep.export_ch8_metros` tables, since they contain the necessary information.

```sql
SELECT
    cbsa_title 'City',
    CAST(median_home AS REAL) * 1000 AS median_home_price_thousands
FROM
    doorstep.ch8_metros
WHERE
    cbsa_title IN ('Ogden, UT', 'Ocala, FL')
    AND year = 2023
ORDER BY
    median_home_price_thousands DESC;
```

This query does the following:
1. It selects the `cbsa_title` (which is the city name) and multiplies the `median_home` by 1000 to convert it from dollars to thousands.
2. It filters the data to include only cities in 2023.
3. It orders the results in descending order by the `median_home_price_thousands` to show the city with the highest median home price first.

Let's walk through the question and the database.

1. **Understand the Task**: We need to compare the renter cost burden share between Toledo and Ann Arbor, MI for the year 2009. The renter cost burden share is represented by the `renter_burdened_share` column in the `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table.

2. **Identify the Relevant Tables**: 
   - The `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table is relevant because it contains the renter cost burden share data.
   - We need to filter the data for 2009 and the cities `Toledo` and `Ann Arbor`.

3. **Construct the SQL Query**:
   - Use a `SELECT` statement to retrieve the `renter_burdened_share` column for the specified cities in the year 2009.
   - Use a `WHERE` clause to filter the data for Toledo (`cbsa_title = 'Toledo, OH'`) and Ann Arbor (`cbsa_title = 'Ann Arbor, MI'`).
   - Use a `GROUP BY` clause to aggregate the results by `cbsa_title` to ensure we get the total renter cost burden

```sql
SELECT 
  cbsa_title AS warehouse, 
  SUM(renter_burdened_share) AS renter_cost_burden_share
FROM 
  doorstep.mart_national_year
WHERE 
  year = 2009 AND 
  cbsa_title IN ('Toledo, OH', 'Ann Arbor, MI')
GROUP BY 
  cbsa_title
ORDER BY 
  renter_cost_burden_share DESC
LIMIT 1
```

```sql
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN t1.renter_burdened_share > t2.renter_burdened_share THEN 'Toledo, OH'
        ELSE 'Ann Arbor, MI'
    END AS warehouse,
    t1.renter_burdened_share AS burdened_share
FROM
    doorstep.ch8_metros AS t1
JOIN
    doorstep.ch8_metros AS t2
ON
    t1.cbsa_code = t2.cbsa_code AND t1.year = t2.year AND t1.cbsa_title IN ('Ann Arbor, MI', 'Toledo, OH')
WHERE
    t1.year = 2009;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN t2.renter_burdened_share > t1.renter_burdened_share THEN t2.renter_burdened_share
        ELSE t1.renter_burdened_share
    END AS renter_burdened_share
FROM 
    doorstep.mart_metro_year AS t1
JOIN 
    doorstep.mart_metro_year AS t2 ON t1.cbsa_code = t2.cbsa_code
WHERE 
    t1.year = 2009 AND t2.year = 2009 AND t1.cbsa_title = 'Ann Arbor, MI' AND t2.cbsa_title = 'Toledo, OH';
```

FROM doorstep.mart_metro_year AS T1
JOIN doorstep.calc_metros AS T2 ON T1.cbsa_code = T2.cbsa_code
WHERE T2.year = 2011
ORDER BY T1.median_income DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN T1.median_income > T2.median_income THEN 'New Orleans'
    ELSE 'Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV'
  END AS Name,
  T1.median_income
FROM 
  doorstep.mart_metro_year AS T1
JOIN 
  doorstep.ch5_ranking AS T2 ON T1.cbsa_code = T2.cbsa_code AND T1.year = T2.year
WHERE 
  T1.year = 2011
  AND T1.cbsa_title IN ('New Orleans-Metairie, LA', 'Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV')
ORDER BY 
  T1.median_income DESC
LIMIT 1;

```sql
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN log_alerts = MAX(log_alerts) THEN 'rapid_movement'
        WHEN log_alerts = MAX(log_alerts) THEN 'round_tripping'
        ELSE 'REFUSE' WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY log_alerts DESC) AND REASON = 'OUT_OF_SCOPE'
    END AS higher_alerts
FROM
    ledger.f05_rule_scorecard;
```

```sql
SELECT CASE 
          WHEN T1.alerts > T2.alerts THEN 'round_trip'
          WHEN T1.alerts < T2.alerts THEN 'rapid_movement'
          ELSE 'equal'
        END AS round_trip_rapid_movement
FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard AS T1
JOIN ledger.models_aml_triage_alerts_scored AS T2
ON T1.rule = T2.rule
ORDER BY round_trip_rapid_movement DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN rule = 'rapid_movement' THEN true_positive ELSE 0 END) AS rapid_movement_alerts,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rule = 'round_tripping' THEN true_positive ELSE 0 END) AS round_tripping_alerts,
       CASE WHEN rapid_movement_alerts > round_tripping_alerts THEN 'rapid_movement' ELSE 'round_tripping' END AS more_alerts
FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN rule = 'round_tripping' THEN SUM(true_positive) 
        WHEN rule = 'rapid_movement' THEN SUM(true_positive)
    END AS total_true_positives,
    rule AS label,
    'count' AS category
FROM 
    ledger.f05_rule_scorecard
GROUP BY 
    rule
ORDER BY 
    total_true_positives DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

Here's the SQL query:

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN rule = 'rapid_movement' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > SUM(CASE WHEN rule = 'round_tripping' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) THEN 'rapid_movement'
        ELSE 'round_tripping'
    END AS alert_type,
    COUNT(*) AS num_alerts
FROM 
    ledger.f05_rule_scorecard
WHERE 
    rule IN ('rapid_movement', 'round_tripping')
GROUP BY 
    alert_type
ORDER BY 
    num_alerts DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT warehouse, SUM(alerts) AS total_alerts
FROM (
    SELECT 'rapid_movement' AS warehouse, SUM(alerts) AS alerts FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard WHERE rule = 'rapid_movement'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'round_trip' AS warehouse, SUM(alerts) AS alerts FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard WHERE rule = 'round_tripping'
) AS subquery
GROUP BY warehouse
ORDER BY total_alerts DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN T1.alerts > T2.alerts THEN 'round trip'
        WHEN T1.alerts < T2.alerts THEN 'rapid movement'
        ELSE 'EQUALS'
    END AS result,
    T1.alerts AS rapid_movement_count,
    T2.alerts AS round_trip_count
FROM 
    ledger.f05_rule_scorecard AS T1
JOIN 
    (SELECT 
        rule,
        SUM(alerts) AS alerts
    FROM 
        ledger.models_aml_triage_alerts_scored
    GROUP BY 
        rule) AS T2
ON 
    T1.rule = T2.rule
ORDER BY 
    rapid_movement_count DESC, 
    round_trip_count DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT CASE 
            WHEN rule_rapid_movement > rule_round_tripping THEN 'rapid_movement'
            WHEN rule_round_tripping > rule_rapid_movement THEN 'round_tripping'
            ELSE 'No such measure'
          END AS alert_source,
          COUNT(*) AS num_alerts
FROM ledger.f05_rule_scorecard
GROUP BY alert_source
ORDER BY num_alerts DESC
LIMIT 1
```

```sql
SELECT

    WHEN t1.price_to_income > t2.price_to_income THEN 'HIGH'
    WHEN t1.price_to_income < t2.price_to_income THEN 'LOW'
    ELSE 'EQUAL'
  END AS price_to_income_ratio_higher,
  t1.cbsa_title AS cbsa_title
FROM
  doorstep.mart_metro_year t1
JOIN
  doorstep.fct_metro_year t2
ON
  t1.cbsa_code = t2.cbsa_code AND t1.year = t2.year AND t1.year = 2012
WHERE
  t2.year = 2012

    doorstep.ch1_national_series rush

    rush.year = 2012 AND rush.metros IN ('Louisville/Jefferson County, KY-IN', 'Canton-Massillon, OH')

Let's walk through the question and the available data.

To answer this question, we need to find the risk-based capital ratio for the 2024 Q4 period in the ledger metrics_bank_month table. The risk-based capital ratio is a measure of the risk associated with the bank's assets, typically calculated as the ratio of risk-weighted assets to average assets.

Step 1: Identify the relevant table and columns.
The relevant table is ledger.metrics_bank_month, and the relevant columns are nim (risk-weighted assets) and average_assets (average assets).

Step 2: Filter the data for the 2024 Q4 period.
We need to filter the data to include only rows where the period is 2024 Q4.

Step 3: Calculate the risk-based capital ratio.
The risk-based capital ratio is calculated as nim divided by average_assets.

```sql
SELECT nim, average_assets, nim / average_assets AS risk_based_capital_ratio
FROM ledger.metrics_bank_month
WHERE period = '2024 Q4';

Let's walk through the question and the data.

To answer this question, we need to:
1. Identify the relevant tables: `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` for capital ratio and `doorstep.mart_metro_year` for quarter information.
2. Join the two tables based on the `period` column in `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` and the `quarters_at` column in `doorstep.mart_metro_year`.
3. Filter the joined table for rows where the `period` is between '2024 Q1' and '2025 Q2'.
4. Order the filtered rows by the `quarters_at` column in ascending order.
5. Select the `quarters_at` column from the filtered rows.

Here is the SQL query that accomplishes this:

```sql
SELECT t1.quarters_at AS quarter
FROM ledger.metrics_bank_quarter t1
JOIN doorstep.mart_metro_year t2 ON t1.period = t2.quarters_at
WHERE t1.period BETWEEN '2024 Q1' AND '2025 Q2'
ORDER BY t2.quarters_at;
```

SELECT q.period FROM (
  SELECT quarter_quarters AS period, quarter_quarters / 4 AS quarter_from TO quarter_quarters / 4 + 3 AS quarter_to
  FROM doorstep.fct_metro_year
  WHERE year BETWEEN 2024 AND 2025
    AND quarter_quarters IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
) q
JOIN (
  SELECT quarter_quarters, capital_ratio
  FROM ledger.metrics_bank_quarter
  WHERE year BETWEEN 2024 AND 2025
    AND quarter_quarters IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
) l
ON q.quarter_from <= l.quarter_quarters AND q.quarter_to >= l.quarter_quarters
WHERE l.capital_ratio > 0.19;

```sql
SELECT AVG(T1.mean_arr_delay) AS average_mean_arrival_delay
FROM turnaround.export_ch8_by_hour AS T1
JOIN turnaround.export_ch8_by_dow AS T2 ON T1.day = T2.day
JOIN turnaround.export_ch8_by_carrier AS T3 ON T2.airport = T3.airport
WHERE T3.carrier IN ('AS', 'NK', 'WN') AND T2.year = 2020
GROUP BY T1.day;
```

```sql
SELECT AVG(CAST(t1.mean_arr_delay AS REAL)) AS average_mean_arrival_delay
FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month t1
JOIN doorstep.export_ch8_by_dow t2 ON t1.carrier = t2.carrier
WHERE t1.year = 2020 AND t1.carrier IN ('AS', 'NK', 'WN')
```

Explanation:
1. The `JOIN` statement combines rows from `turnaround.mart_carrier_month` (aliased as `t1`) and `doorkstep.export_ch8_by_dow` (aliased as `t2`) on the `carrier` column.
2. The `WHERE` clause filters the records to include rows from 2020 and with carriers 'AS', 'NK', or 'WN'.
3. The `AVG` function calculates the average of the `mean_arr_delay` column from `turnaround.mart_carrier_month`.
4. The result is cast to a REAL type to ensure the average is calculated with decimal precision instead of integer precision.

```sql
SELECT AVG(airport) AS airport, AVG(mean_arr_delay) AS mean_arr_delay
FROM turnaround.mart_airport_day
WHERE (carrier = 'AS' OR carrier = 'NK' OR carrier = 'WN') AND year = 2020;
```

This query calculates the mean share of flights cancelled by Envoy, SkyWest Airlines, and Republic Airways in 2025. The formula calculates the difference in scheduled departures divided by the sum of scheduled departures, then converts it to a percentage of total scheduled departures. The WHERE clause ensures that only the calls for Envoy, SkyWest Airlines, and Republic Airways in 2025 are considered.

        cbsa_title AS metro,
        YEAR AS year,
        SUM(CASE WHEN cancelled > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / SUM(flown) AS cancelled_percent

        doorstep.fct_metro_year
    WHERE
        year = 2025
        AND airport IN ('DTW', 'LAX', 'MIA')

        metro
),

    SELECT
        metro,
        100 * cancelled_percent AS cancelled_percent

    cancelled_percent AS share

Let's walk through the question and the query.

To answer this question, we need to:
1. Select the year from the `turnaround` table.
2. Filter the rows where the `carrier` is 'HA' and the `on_time` performance is above 85 percent.

The SQL query is:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT T1.year
FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T1
WHERE T1.carrier = 'HA' AND T1.on_time > 0.85;
```

Explanation:
- `SELECT DISTINCT T1.year`: This selects unique years from the `turnaround` table.
- `FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T1`: This specifies the table as `turnaround.mart_carrier_month` and aliases it as `T1`.
- `WHERE T1.carrier = 'HA'`: This filters the rows where the `carrier` column is 'HA'.
- `AND T1.on_time > 0.85`: This filters the rows where the `on_time` column is above 85 percent.

This query will return the years from 2020 to 2024 where the on time performance in Hawaiian Airlines was above 85 percent.

Let's walk through the question and the database

1. **Identify the Relevant Tables**: The question involves average arrival delays, so we need data from the `turnaround.mart_carrier_month` table. This table contains information about each carrier's average arrival delay in each month and year.

2. **Filter by Year and Aggregate**: We are interested in 2016, so we filter the data for `year = 2016`. We then calculate the average arrival delay for each carrier.

3. **Order and Limit**: We order the results by the average arrival delay in descending order to get the top carriers first. We limit the output to 10 carriers to avoid the result set being too large.

Here's the SQL query to answer the question:

```sql
SELECT 
    carrier,
    AVG(arr_delay_sum) / SUM(flown) * 1000 AS avg_arr_delay_mins
FROM 
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
WHERE 
    year = 2016
GROUP BY 
    carrier
ORDER BY 
    avg_arr_delay_mins DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

```sql
SELECT
    TransformedPeriod AS Year,
    CAST(TransformedMeanArrivalDelay AS DOUBLE) AS MeanArrivalDelay
FROM (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', Flight_Date) AS Year,
        AVG(CASE WHEN Mean_Arrival_Delay > 8.8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Mean_ArrivalDelay,
        Flight_Date
    FROM
        turnaround.export_ch8_by_date
    WHERE
        airport = 'ATL'
        AND Flight_Date >= '2017-01-01'
        AND Flight_Date <= '2021-12-31'
    GROUP BY
        Flight_Date
) AS TransformedData
ORDER BY
    Mean_ArrivalDelay DESC;

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE WHEN "Hispanic or Latino" > "Other or joint" THEN "Hispanic or Latino" ELSE "Other or joint" END AS group,
  CASE WHEN "White non Hispanic" > "Hispanic or Latino" THEN "White non Hispanic" ELSE "Hispanic or Latino" END AS group2,
  CAST(T1.rate AS DOUBLE) AS rate
FROM 
  ledger.f03_unadjusted AS T1
JOIN 
  doorstep.ch1_national_series AS T2 ON T1.group = T2.group
WHERE 
  T1.group = 'Hispanic or Latino' OR T1.group = 'Other or joint' OR T1.group = 'White non Hispanic'
GROUP BY 
  group, group2, T1.rate

2. **Join Tables**: We need to join the `ledger` and `doorkstep.fct_metro_year` tables based on the `cbsa_code` and `year` columns.

3. **Calculate Return on Average Assets**: The return on average assets (ROAA) is calculated as `(net_income / total_assets) * 100`.

4. **Filter Quarters and Quarters at**: We need to filter the quarters between 2024 Q1 and 2025 Q3. We also need to filter the quarters at.

5. **Filter ROAA Higher than 1 Percent**: We need to filter the rows where the ROAA is higher than 1 percent.

Let's walk through the question and the database.

The goal is to find the number of metros with an anchored median home value above $170,000 in 2009. Here's a step-by-step approach to derive the SQL query:

1. **Identify the relevant table**: The `export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity` table contains information about the anchored median home value for each metro in the US.

2. **Filter the data**: We need to filter the data for the year 2009 and the anchored median home value above $170,000.

3. **Count the metros**: Finally, we need to count the number of metros that meet the criteria.

However, the `export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity` table does not directly contain the anchored median home value. It contains information about the current sensitivity of the anchored median home value, not the historical data. To get the historical data, we need to join the `export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity` table with the `export_ch6_by_year` table.

1. **Join the tables**: We join the `export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity` table with the `export_ch6_by_year` table on the `anchor_year` column.

Let's use the `doorstep` database with the following SQL query to find the average median home value across Lakeland-Winter Haven, FL, Lansing and New York in 2006.

```sql
SELECT 
    a.cbsa_title,
    AVG(a.median_value_reported) as median_home_value
FROM 
    doorstep.mart_metro_year a
JOIN 
    doorstep.export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity s ON a.cbsa_code = s.metros
WHERE 
    s.Anchor_year = 2006
    AND a.cbsa_title IN ('Lakeland-Winter Haven, FL', 'Lansing-East Lansing, MI', 'New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ')
GROUP BY 
    a.cbsa_title;
```

This query joins the `mart_metro_year` table with the `export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity` table on the `metros` column, which is used by both tables to identify the same United States metro area. It filters the results to only include metros with an anchor year of 2006 and those that are in Lakeland-Winter Haven, FL, Lansing, or New York. Finally, it calculates the average `median_value

```sql
SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN cbsa_title = 'Lakeland-Winter Haven, FL' THEN median_home ELSE NULL END) AS lakeland_winterhaven,
       AVG(CASE WHEN cbsa_title = 'Lansing-East Lansing, MI' THEN median_home ELSE NULL END) AS lansing,
       AVG(CASE WHEN cbsa_title = 'New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ' THEN median_home ELSE NULL END) AS new_york
FROM doorstep.mart_metro_year
WHERE year = 2006;
```

    SELECT
        mule as rule,
        round_trip as rule,
        structuring as rule,
        SUM(alert_id) / count(*) as mean_alerts
    FROM
        ledger.models_aml_triage_alerts_scored
    WHERE
        rule = 'mule' OR rule = 'round_tripping' OR rule = 'structuring'
    GROUP BY
        rule
)

    'forecast' AS label,
    REFUSE AS reason_code
FROM

        median_rent_share AS current_median_rent_share
    FROM
        doorstep.mart_metro_year
    WHERE
        cbsa_title = 'Urban Honolulu, HI' AND

    cbsa_code,
    CASE
        WHEN current_median_rent_share < next_year_median_rent_share THEN 'UP'
        WHEN current_median_rent_share > next_year_median_rent_share THEN 'DOWN'
        ELSE 'STAY'
    END AS renter_cost_burden_share_change
FROM

WITH CurrentYearPermits AS (
  SELECT permits
  FROM doorstep.cbsa
  WHERE kind = 'single_family' AND cbsa_title = 'Fresno, CA'
    AND year = (SELECT MAX(year) FROM doorstep.cbsa WHERE kind = 'single_family' AND cbsa_title = 'Fresno, CA')
),
NextYearPermits AS (
  SELECT permits
  FROM doorstep.cbsa
  WHERE kind = 'single_family' AND cbsa_title = 'Fresno, CA'
    AND year = (SELECT MAX(year) + 1 FROM doorstep.cbsa WHERE kind = 'single_family' AND cbsa_title = 'Fresno, CA')
)

FROM CurrentYearPermits
JOIN NextYearPermits ON 1 = 1

    CASE 
        WHEN doorstep.fct_metro_year.cbsa_title LIKE 'Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD' THEN 'Philadelphia'
        ELSE REFUSE('OUT_OF_SCOPE')

        ELSE 'NO'

```sql
WITH QuarterReturns AS (
    SELECT
        t2.year AS year,
        quarter AS quarter,
        AVG(t1.roa) * 100 AS roa_percent
    FROM
        ledger.metrics_bank_quarter AS t1
    INNER JOIN
        doorstep.fct_metro_year AS t2
    ON
        t2.year = t1.period AND t2.quarters_at = t1.quarters_at AND t2.cbsa_code = t1.cbsa_code AND t2.cbsa_title = t1.cbsa_title
    WHERE
        t1.period BETWEEN '2024 Q2' AND '2026 Q2'
    GROUP BY
        t2.year,
        quarter
),
SortedReturns AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        quarter,
        roa_percent
    FROM
        QuarterReturns
    ORDER BY
        roa_percent ASC
    LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
    year,
    quarter,
    CAST(roa_percent AS REAL) * 100 AS roa_percent
FROM
    SortedReturns;
```

2. Identify the top 3 metros with the highest payment shares.

Here's the SQL query to achieve this:

```sql

FROM doorstep.mart_metro_year
WHERE year = 2014
ORDER BY payment_share DESC
LIMIT 3;

This query does the following:
- Selects the `metro` and `payment_share` columns from the `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table.
- Filters the results to include only rows where the `year` is 2014.
- Orders the results in descending order based on the `payment_share`.
- Limits the results to the top 3 rows.

This query will give us the top 3 metros with the highest payment shares in 2014.

Let's approach this step by step:

2. **Filter by year**: We need to filter the data for the year 2005.

3. **Count renter households**: We need to count the number of renter households in each metro.

4. **Order by count in descending order**: To find the metros with the highest count, we order the results by the count in descending order.

5. **Limit to top 5 metros**: Since we are asked for the top 5 metros, we limit the results to the top 5 rows.

Here's the SQL query to achieve this:

```sql

1. **Identify the relevant tables**: The information about flights and delays is in the `turnaround.mart_carrier_month` table.
2. **Filter by the year 2016**: We need to look at data from the year 2016 to find the lowest average arrival delay.
3. **Calculate the average arrival delay**: We need to compute the average arrival delay for each carrier.
4. **Order the carriers by average delay**: We need to arrange the carriers in ascending order based on their average arrival delay.

Here's the SQL query that accomplishes this:

```sql
SELECT
    carrier,
    AVG(arr_delay_sum) AS avg_arr_delay
FROM
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month
WHERE
    year = 2016
GROUP BY
    carrier
ORDER BY
    avg_arr_delay ASC
LIMIT 3;

- **SELECT**: We select the `carrier` and calculate the average of the `arr_delay_sum` column, alias it as `avg_arr_delay`.

- **WHERE**: We filter the data to only include rows

2. **Sort by cancellation rate**: We want to find the lowest cancellation rate, so we order the results by `cancelled` in ascending order (`ASC`).

3. **Limit the output**: We only need the top 3 carriers, so we use the LIMIT clause.

4. **Select the required columns**: We only need the `carrier` and `cancelled` columns, both of which are in the `turnaround` table.

5. **Cast the `cancelled` column to a fraction**: Since the `cancelled` column is currently a count of flights, we need to cast it to a fraction to get the lowest cancellation rate.

Therefore, the final SQL query is:

```sql

Let's approach this step-by-step:

We need to find the quarters with the highest Nim values between 2023 Q4 and 2026 Q2. Here's how we can do it:

1. **Join the tables**: We need to join the `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` table with the `ledger.f01_ratios_monthly` table on the `months` column, which is common to both tables.

2. **Filter by date range**: We need to filter the data to include only the quarters from 2023 Q4 to 2026 Q2.

3. **Group by quarter**: We need to group the results by the `months` column to find the highest Nim value for each quarter.

4. **Order by Nim in descending order**: We need to order the results by the `nim` column in descending order to get the quarters with the highest Nim values at the top.

5. **Limit to 5 quarters**: We need to limit the results to only the 5 quarters with the highest Nim values.

6. **Select the required columns**: We need to select the `months` column to find the quarters with the highest Nim.

Here's the SQL query that implements these steps

```sql
SELECT t1.month, t1.nim_ratio
FROM (
    SELECT month, nim_ratio
    FROM ledger.f01_ratios_monthly
    WHERE nim_ratio = (SELECT MAX(nim_ratio) FROM ledger.f01_ratios_monthly)
      AND month BETWEEN '2023-04' AND '2026-02'
) t1
ORDER BY t1.nim_ratio DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

Let's walk through the question and the data:

To answer this question, we need to:
1. Select the period, quarter, and NPL ratio columns from the `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` table.
2. Filter the data for the years 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026.
3. Order the results by the NPL ratio in descending order to get the quarters with the highest NPL ratio at the top.
4. Limit the results to the top 3 quarters.

Here's the SQL query to achieve this:

```sql
SELECT
    period,
    quarter,
    round(npl_ratio * 100, 2) AS npl_ratio_percent -- Convert to percentage
FROM
    ledger.metrics_bank_quarter
WHERE
    year BETWEEN 2023 AND 2026
ORDER BY
    npl_ratio_percent DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

This query will return the period, quarter, and the NPL ratio as a percentage for the top 3 quarters from 2023 Q4 to 2026 Q2 with the highest NPL ratio.

    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM YEAR) AS year,
        SUM(PERIOD SHARE) AS national_payment_share
    FROM
        doorstep.export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity
    WHERE
        Anchor YEAR BETWEEN 2006 AND 2024
    GROUP BY
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM YEAR)
)
SELECT
    year,
    national_payment_share
FROM
    NationalPaymentShares
ORDER BY
    national_payment_share DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT year, latest_payment_share
FROM (
  SELECT year,
         latest_payment_share,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY latest_payment_share DESC) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT anchor_year,
                     latest_payment_share,
                     2006 AS year,
                     latest_payment_share AS latest_payment_share
    FROM doorstep.export_ch1_anchor_sensitivity
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DISTINCT metro AS anchor_year,
                     latest_payment_share,
                     2006 AS year,
                     latest_payment_share AS latest_payment_share
    FROM doorstep.export_ch8_largest
  ) AS subquery
  WHERE anchor_year >= 2006 AND anchor_year <= 2024
) AS ranked_years
WHERE rn <= 3;
```

Q2_to_Q4_2026 AS (
    SELECT period, efficiency_ratio
    FROM ledger.f01_ratios_monthly
    WHERE year = 2026 AND month IN ('Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4')
),
Combined AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT T1.period, T2.efficiency_ratio
    FROM Q2_to_Q4_2024 AS T1
    JOIN Q2_to_Q4_2026 AS T2 ON T1.period = T2.period

WITH quarter_range AS (

    cbsa_title,

    quarter,

    year BETWEEN 2024 AND 2026
    AND quarter >= 2

    cbsa_code,
    cbsa_title,
    kind,
    year,
    quarter
),
lowest_profits AS (
  SELECT 
    cbsa_code,
    period,
    profit / 1000 AS profit_thousands

  period,
  profit_thousands
FROM

Let's walk through the question and the data.

1. **Identify the Relevant Tables and Columns**: The question asks for the lowest ROA values in 2023 Q4 to 2026 Q2. From the `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` table, we need the `roa` column that represents the return on assets (RoA) as a percentage. Also, we need the `quarter` column to filter the quarters within the specified range.

2. **Filter the Data**: We need to filter the data to include only the quarters from 2023 Q4 to 2026 Q2. This can be done using the `WHERE` clause with the `quarter` column.

3. **Order the Data**: We need to order the filtered data by the `roa` column in ascending order so that the quarters with the lowest RoA values appear first.

4. **Limit the Results**: Since we only need the top 3 quarters with the lowest RoA values, we use the `LIMIT` clause with a value of 3.

The SQL query to achieve this is:

```sql
SELECT period, roa * 100 AS roa_percentage
FROM ledger.metrics_bank_quarter

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT quarter, period, CASE WHEN roa_is_percent THEN roa * 100 ELSE roa END AS roa_percentage
FROM (
  SELECT
    cbsa_code,
    year,
    quarter,
    period,
    CASE
      WHEN nim_low <= min(nim) AND efficiency_ratio_low <= min(efficiency_ratio) AND roa_low <= min(roa) AND npl_ratio_low <= min(npl_ratio) THEN 'lowest'
      ELSE 'higher'
    END AS roa_is_percent,
    nim,
    efficiency_ratio,
    roa,
    npl_ratio
  FROM
    ledger.metrics_bank_quarter
  WHERE
    year BETWEEN 2023 AND 2026
    AND quarter BETWEEN 4 AND 2
    AND period IN ('Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4')
) AS subquery
ORDER BY
  quarter
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
SELECT 
    T1.year, 
    T1.quarter, 
    T1.period, 
    T1.roa * 100 AS roa_percent
FROM

JOIN 
    ledger.f01_ratios_monthly AS T2 ON T1.cbsa_code = T2.cbsa_code AND T1.year = T2.period AND T1.quarter = T2.month
WHERE 
    T1.year >= 2023 AND T1.year <= 2026 AND T1.quarter >= 4 AND T1.quarter <= 2
ORDER BY 
    T1.roa_percent ASC
LIMIT 3;
```

 lowest_quarters AS (

    period_statistics

Let's walk through the question and the database.

1. **Identify the Relevant Tables**: We need to focus on the `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` table for total deposits and the `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table for the quarter information.

2. **Determine the Filter Condition**: We need to find the quarters between 2024 Q3 and 2026 Q2. This can be achieved by filtering the `quarter_at` column in the `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table.

3. **Join the Tables**: We will join the `ledger.metrics_bank_quarter` table with the `doorstep.mart_metro_year` table on the `cbsa_code` column to get the corresponding quarter information.

4. **Filter the Data**: We will filter the data to include only the quarters between 2024 Q3 and 2026 Q2.

5. **Calculate the Total Deposits**: We will calculate the total deposits for each quarter.

6. **Order the Results**: We will order the results by the total deposits in descending order.

7. **Limit the Results**: We will limit the results to the top 3 quarters.

This query will return the average efficiency ratio for the periods 2025 Q2 and 2026 Q2. ```sql
WITH cancelled_flights AS (
    SELECT 
        CAST(count AS DOUBLE) / Sum(count) AS ratio
    FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month
    WHERE year BETWEEN 2016 and 2019
      AND airport = 'DTW'
      AND cancelled > 0
),
rolling_up AS (
    SELECT 
        year - 1 AS prev_year,
        CAST(cnt AS DOUBLE) / SUM(cnt) AS ratio
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            count AS cnt, 
            CAST(CASE WHEN year = 2016 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS INT) AS new_year
        FROM turnaround.mart_carrier_month
        WHERE year BETWEEN 2016 and 2019
          AND airport = 'DTW'
          AND cancelled > 0
    ) AS subquery
    GROUP BY new_year, prev_year
)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN ratio > rolling_up.ratio THEN 'up'
        ELSE 'down'
    END AS share_change,
    AVG(ratio) AS average_share_change
FROM cancelled_flights
JOIN rolling_up ON cancelled_flights.year - 1 = rolling_up.prev_year;
```

```sql
WITH La_Crosse AS (
    SELECT year, renter_burdened_share
    FROM doorstep.mart_metro_year
    WHERE cbsa_title = 'La Crosse-Onalaska, WI-MN'
    AND year BETWEEN 2006 AND 2021

    SELECT year, renter_burdened_share AS base_share,

```sql

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN T2.cancellation_rate > T1.cancellation_rate THEN 'UP'
    WHEN T2.cancellation_rate < T1.cancellation_rate THEN 'DOWN'
    ELSE 'SAME'
  END AS change_type,
  'Hawaii Airlines' AS carrier,
  SUM(T2.cancellation_rate - T1.cancellation_rate) * 100 / MAX(T2.cancellation_rate) AS change_percentage
FROM 
  turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T1
INNER JOIN 
  turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T2 ON T1.carrier = T2.carrier AND T1.year = T2.year AND T1.month = T2.month
WHERE 
  T1.year >= 2017 AND T1.year <= 2025;
```

```sql
SELECT
    'HAW' AS warehouse,
    CASE WHEN (t1.canceled - t2.canceled) / ((t1.canceled + t2.canceled) / 2) * 100 > 0 THEN 'UP' ELSE 'DOWN' END AS change
FROM
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month t1
JOIN
    turnaround.mart_carrier_month t2
ON
    t1.year = t2.year AND t1.carrier = t2.carrier AND t1.month = t2.month AND t1.crs_elapsed_sum - t2.crs_elapsed_sum > 0
WHERE
    t1.year BETWEEN 2017 AND 2025
GROUP BY
    'HAW';
```

```sql
SELECT 
    CASE WHEN cancel_rate_quarters > 0 THEN (cancel_rate_quarters / total_originations) * 100 - 100 ELSE cancel_rate_quarters END AS cancellation_rate_increase
FROM (
    SELECT 
        cbsa_code, 
        year, 
        cast(sum(cancelled) as REAL) as cancel_rate_quarters, 
        count(*) as total_originations
    FROM 
        turnaround.mart_carrier_month
    WHERE 
        carrier = 'HA' AND year BETWEEN 2017 AND 2025
    GROUP BY 
        cbsa_code, year
    ORDER BY 
        cbsa_code, year
) AS subquery
WHERE 
    cancellation_rate_increase IS NOT NULL;
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN T2.On_time > T3.On_time THEN 'RISING'
    WHEN T2.On_time < T3.On_time THEN 'FALLING'
    ELSE 'STABLE'
  END AS share_change
FROM 
  turnaround.export_ch3_by_carrier AS T1
JOIN 
  turnaround.mart_carrier_month AS T2
ON 
  T1.Carrier = T2.carrier AND T1.Year = T2.year AND T1.month = T2.month

  turnaround.export_ch3_by_carrier AS T3

  T3.Carrier = T1.Carrier AND T3.Year = T3.year AND T3.month = T3.month

```

```sql
WITH year_data AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN year = 2022 THEN '2022'
            WHEN year = 2024 THEN '2024'
            ELSE REFUSE 'OUT_OF_RANGE'
        END AS year,
        CAST(CASE WHEN on_time / scheduled * 100 > 95 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS DOUBLE) AS on_time_share
    FROM
        turnaround.export_ch5_ranking
    WHERE
        carrier = 'UA'
        AND year = 2022 OR year = 2024
)
SELECT
    year,
    SUM(on_time_share) AS total_on_time_share
FROM
    year_data
GROUP BY
    year
HAVING
    total_on_time_share / COUNT(*) > 0.5;
```

```sql
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN efficiency_ratio_2024_Q2 > efficiency_ratio_2025_Q3 THEN 'Rise'
    WHEN efficiency_ratio_2024_Q2 < efficiency_ratio_2025_Q3 THEN 'Fall'
    ELSE 'REFUSE'
  END AS efficiency_ratio_change,
  'percent' AS unit
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      efficiency_ratio_2025_Q3 AS efficiency_ratio_2025_Q3,
      efficiency_ratio_2024_Q2 AS efficiency_ratio_2024_Q2
    FROM 
      ledger.f01_ratios_monthly
    WHERE 
      first_month = '2025-03-01'
  ) AS ratios
WHERE 
  ratios.efficiency_ratio_2024_Q2 >= 0 AND ratios.efficiency_ratio_2025_Q3 >= 0;

```sql
with cancelled_rate_changes as (
  select
    airport,
    year,
    rate_quarters
  from
    turnaround.mart_airport_day
  where
    airport = 'LGA'
    and year between 2016 and 2025
),
rate_changes as (
  select
    year,
    COALESCE(coalesce(max_rate, 0) - min_rate, 0) as rate_change,
    COALESCE(coalesce(max_rate, 0) * 100.0 / min_rate, 0) as rate_change_percent
  from (
    select
      year,
      max(rate_quarters) as max_rate,
      min(rate_quarters) as min_rate
    from
      cancelled_rate_changes
    group by
      year
  ) as subquery
)
select
  year,
  rate_change_percent
from
  rate_changes
order by
  year;
```

Let's walk through the question and the data.

To answer this question, we need to calculate the national payment share for each year between 2005 and 2022 and then find the change in this share.

1. **Select the relevant columns**: We need the year, the payment share, and the national payment share (which is the payment share for the United States).

2. **Filter for the years**: We need to filter the data to only include years between 2005 and 2022.

3. **Calculate the national payment share**: We can calculate the national payment share by summing up all the payment shares in the United States and then dividing by the total number of metro areas.

4. **Calculate the change in payment share**: We can calculate the change in payment share by subtracting the national payment share in 2005 from the national payment share in 2022.

5. **Order the results**: We need to order the results by the year to show the change in payment share for each year.

6. **Select the required columns**: We only need to select the year, the payment share, and the national payment share.

Here's the SQL query to achieve this:

```

Let's examine the data in the `ledger.f01_ratios_monthly` table to answer this question.

1. We need to find the efficiency ratios for the period 2024 Q2 and 2026 Q1.
2. We can filter the data to include only rows where the year is 2024 and the quarter is Q2, and where the year is 2026 and the quarter is Q1.
3. We then calculate the difference between the two efficiency ratios.

Here's the SQL query to achieve this:

```sql

    CASE 
        WHEN y2024_q2 EFF_RATIO > y2026_q1_eff_ratio THEN 'Rised'
        WHEN y2024_q2_eff_RATIO < y2026_q1_eff_ratio THEN 'Falling'
        ELSE 'No Change'
    END AS efficiency_ratio_change
FROM 
    ledger.f01_ratios_monthly

                 SUM(cancelled) / SUM(flown) * 100 AS cancellation_rate,

```sql

```sql
WITH ratio_change AS (
    SELECT
        period,
        capital_ratio,
        LAG(capital_ratio) OVER (ORDER BY period) AS prev_capital_ratio,
        CASE
            WHEN prev_capital_ratio IS NULL THEN 0
            ELSE (capital_ratio - prev_capital_ratio) / prev_capital_ratio * 100
        END AS change_percentage
    FROM
        ledger.metrics_bank_month
    WHERE
        period = '2024 Q1'
        OR period = '2024 Q3'
)
SELECT
    period,
    IF(change_percentage > 0, 'Rise', 'Fall') AS capital_ratio_change,
    change_percentage AS capital_ratio_change_percentage
FROM
    ratio_change
WHERE
    period BETWEEN '2024 Q1' AND '2024 Q3';
```

```sql
SELECT

    WHEN t1.mean_arrival_delay_2021 < t1.mean_arrival_delay_2016 THEN 'FALL'
    ELSE 'STABLE'
  END AS rise_or_fall
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      AVG(mean_arrival_delay) AS mean_arrival_delay_2016 FROM turnaround.export_ch8_by_year WHERE year = 2016
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
      AVG(mean_arrival_delay) AS mean_arrival_delay_2021 FROM turnaround.export_ch8_by_year WHERE year = 2021
  ) t1
JOIN 
  (
    SELECT carrier, AVG(mean_arrival_delay) AS mean_arrival_delay FROM turnaround.export_ch8_by_carrier_month WHERE carrier = 'WN' GROUP BY carrier
  ) t2 ON t1.carrier = t2.carrier ORDER BY rise_or_fall;

```sql
SELECT T1.renter_burdened_share
FROM (
  SELECT T3.mart_national_year AS year,
         T2.cbsa_title AS cbsa_title,
         (T2.renter_households / T3.households) * 100 AS renter_cost_burden_share
  FROM doorstep.mart_national_year AS T3
  JOIN doorstep.export_ch8_metros AS T2 ON T3.year = T2.year AND T2.cbsa_code = T3.cbsa_code
  WHERE T2.cbsa_title = 'Memphis, TN-MS-AR' AND T3.year = 1980
) AS T1
WHERE T1.year = 1980 AND T1.renter_households IS NOT NULL AND T1.cbsa_title IS NOT NULL AND T1.renter_burdened_share IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY T1.renter_burdened_share DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH payment_share_rank AS (
    SELECT
        cbsa_title AS metro,
        payment_share,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cbsa_title ORDER BY payment_share ASC) AS rank
    FROM
        doorstep.mart_metro_year
    WHERE
        year BETWEEN 2012 AND 2024
),
specific_years AS (
    SELECT
        metro
    FROM
        payment_share_rank
    WHERE
        rank BETWEEN 1 AND 5
)
SELECT
    metro,
    payment_share
FROM
    doorstep.mart_metro_year
WHERE
    metro IN (SELECT metro FROM specific_years) AND year BETWEEN 2012 AND 2024;
```
